## Context / Problem
`tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py:311` patches `binding_store_mod._now_iso` to advance the wall clock, then asserts that an unchanged second reconcile pass rewrites no bytes. The patch is how the test proves the no-churn contract is real rather than a coincidence of a fast test run.

RP-02 S2 T2 moved the absence/tombstone/comment cluster into `binding_lifecycle.py`, so `clear_absent` (and its siblings) now resolve `_now_iso` from `binding_lifecycle`, not `binding_store`. The existing patch therefore no longer reaches them.

## Impact
The test still PASSES, and correctly so — the no-churn contract means the clock is never consulted on a healthy pass. But its blast radius narrowed: it would no longer catch a regression that made `clear_absent` (or another moved operation) stamp `updated_at` unconditionally. That is a silent weakening of an integration-tier oracle.

Coverage did not disappear, it moved tiers: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_lifecycle.py::test_clear_absent_does_not_dirty_an_entry_with_no_absence` pins the contract directly on the policy owner, and was one of the held-out tests for S2 T2. So the risk here is contained, which is why this is a follow-up rather than a blocker.

## Outcome
Restore the integration oracle's original reach by patching the clock on BOTH modules, so it again fails if any binding operation stamps a timestamp on an unchanged pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The idempotency test patches `_now_iso` on `binding_lifecycle` as well as `binding_store` (or on a single shared source, if one is introduced).
- [x] With the patch in place, making `clear_absent` stamp `updated_at` unconditionally drives the integration test RED — verified by seeding that mutation, not assumed. [operator-attested]
- [x] The test still passes unmutated, and still asserts byte-level no-churn across an unchanged second pass.
- [x] Audit the same file for other `binding_store_mod`-targeted patches whose subject moved to `binding_lifecycle.py` during RP-02 S2.

## Notes
Discovered by the implementation subagent during RP-02 S2 T2 and deliberately left alone there: that ticket's instructions forbade touching test files outside its scope, and widening an integration oracle is a test-hygiene change that deserves its own review rather than riding along in an extraction slice.
